item.title: Salsa Thursdays at Time Out Market — Thu Aug 13, 7:00 PM — Time Out Market New York
item.description:
Join us for one of NYC’s best free salsa nights and turn your Thursday into a dance-floor celebration.
Get your salsa on every Thursday night at Time Out Market New York! Head up to the fifth floor for an electrifying evening of rhythm, movement, and Latin vibes. Whether you’re a total beginner or a seasoned dancer, this is your weekly excuse to move, sweat, and smile. Starting at 7:30 PM, renowned instructor Marlene Veras will guide you through the steps, breaking down the fundamentals so you feel confident on the dance floor. The night is powered by infectious beats from DJ Ray Suave, with live percussion by Jessica La Timbalera, setting the stage for a high-energy salsa experience. After the lesson, the floor opens up for a full-on salsa dance party until 10 PM. Bring a partner or come solo—everyone’s welcome.
Source: Go Latin Dance

item.title: 2026 Summer Camps — Fri Aug 14, 12:00 AM — Aga Khan Museum
item.description:
Inspired by the Aga Khan Museum’s collections and current exhibition Game On ! , campers ages 6 to 12 will explore the art, strategy, and creativity behind games from around the world. Throughout the summer, campers will design and build their own games, craft handmade boards and pieces, experiment with puzzles and storytelling, and participate in collaborative challenges that combine creativity, problem-solving, and imagination.
Each week introduces a new theme — from global games and strategy challenges to imaginative storytelling and game design — giving campers the opportunity to create custom board games, sculpt game pieces, build puzzles, invent characters, and test their ideas through playful competition. Through hands-on making, gallery exploration, and outdoor activities, campers will discover how games connect cultures, inspire creativity, and bring people together.
Source: Aga Khan Museum

**A Hidden Ravine, Neighbourhood Trails & Dinner at Pickle Barrel**
Some of Toronto's best walks take you through places you'd never expect.
Join us for a relaxed summer walk that combines peaceful ravines, neighbourhood parks, city pathways, and one of Toronto's best shopping destinations—all in one afternoon.

item.title: DARKFIELD — Fri Aug 21 — The Distillery District
item.description:
DARKFIELD returns to Toronto for six weeks, arriving at the Distillery District from 21 August to 4 October.
You sit down inside a shipping container. The headphones go on. The lights go out. 360-degree sound builds a world around you, one your mind fills in, because it has
nothing to see. Two experiences run side by side, and they are different pieces.
SÉANCE. A seance guided by a medium you'll never see.
FLIGHT. Between takeoff and landing, reality splits.
SÉANCE lasts 20 minutes and FLIGHT lasts 25. Most people book both, see SÉANCE first and FLIGHT afterwards, and have one of our DARKFIELD cocktails in between. Door to door that is about an hour, and booking both costs less than buying them separately. DARKFIELD has toured the UK, Asia, Australia and New Zealand, Turkey and North America. item.title: BOOK LAUNCH: SWEET SORREL STAND, by Yolanda T. Marshall — Mon Aug 24, 11:00 AM — BLACKHURST CULTURAL CENTRE
item.description:
Just when you thought that the summer could not get any sweeter, beloved author Yolanda Marshall and Chalkboard Publishing bring us a new edition of SWEET SORREL STAND! SWEET SORREL STAND celebrates Caribbean culture, entrepreneurship, and family support by showing how two siblings, Rose and Nicolas, turn their love of a traditional sorrel drink into a successful neighbourhood business. This new edition of a Canadian favourite features financial literacy activities to help young readers explore the path of entrepreneurship and, of course, a sorrel drink recipe! Look forward to an exciting presentation including a reading by Yolanda Marshall, activities, snacks, and SO&SO Sorrel and Soda. Guests will have an opportunity to purchase SWEET SORREL STAND, 2nd ed., and have it signed by Yolanda. Free admission. All are welcome. Nothing like a Caribbean story to sweeten up the summer!
Source: A Different Booklist
